## September: direct radio routing to Tiflis

**Sources on this page:** p57 A1, p57 A2, p57 A3. [Concise case study](../radio/september_tiflis_radio_routing.md).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-september-tiflis-radio-routing-september-direct-radio-routing-to-tiflis"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The original page gives one three-part instruction. Reading its actual part boundaries recovers a coherent route and monitoring order under the published key. All repeated place names and call signs remain visible. The page heading is 20 September, the internal header gives 20, and reception is 21 September; those are distinct source dates.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-september-tiflis-radio-routing-p57-a1"></a>

### p57 A1

Observed coordinate changes, with zero-based source indices: **65 G→F**.

Printed-mask fills: **205→G**.

The complete edited stream re-encrypts to exactly the source plus those changes.

**Readable German — complete edited stream with spacing and punctuation only:**

> Vorbehaltlich Genehmigung Akonach sind saemtliche Sprueche fuer Tiflis Tiflis bis auf weiteres von dort direkt blind zu funken.

**Meaning:** Subject to Akonach approval, all messages for Tiflis are to be transmitted directly from there by blind transmission until further notice. The repeated TIFLIS is retained; this is an instruction, not evidence that the transmissions took place.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-september-tiflis-radio-routing-source-annotation-and-conservative-overprint-masks"></a>

### Source annotation and conservative overprint masks

Part 3 has a visible **D above the A** in typed `FGAXF`. The raw transcription
keeps the typed A at source index 132; applying the annotated D costs one
observed-coordinate substitution and changes `2NKUENDIGEN` to `ANKUENDIGEN`.
This source annotation supplies independent support beyond the readable-word
proposal. The [detail image](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/sources/p57_A3_annotation.png)
shows the two glyphs without conflating them into one transcription.

Two other overprints are conservatively masked, not forced to a coordinate:
part 1 source 205 and part 2 source 1. Their proposed G and X fills restore
`FUNKEN` and `SEHR`, respectively. The [overprint crop](../../experiments/september_radio_instructions/sources/p57_A1_A2_overprints.png)
also confirms the clear group `FVAAX`, which directly yields `BLIND` without
an editorial coordinate change.

Part 1 `CPRUECHE→SPRUECHE` costs one substitution. Part 2 `V0N→VON` costs one
substitution: the literal zero in the raw word is visible and its proposed
letter replacement is explicitly counted. The reference digits 652, 4 and 43908
are unchanged.

Part 2 ends `ZUR SICHERSTELLUNG DES`; part 3 begins `MITHOERENS`. The complete
three-part reading therefore states the reason for announcing COS traffic
at agreed times. The words describe requested radio practice, without
establishing whether that practice was carried out.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-september-tiflis-radio-routing-attribution-and-evidence"></a>

### Attribution and evidence

The unchanged published key retains its original recovery credit. Earlier unreviewed repository OCR screens split the p57 parts across the wrong boundaries and did not produce these readable texts; the relevant prior rows are retained. This comparison does not establish an external first-decipherment claim.
